records.name: Bengkulu
records.summary:
No Bengkulu-specific statute, enforcement action, protection or service appears in the audited sources; they establish the national frame a visitor shares here: a 2022 wire report (page unretrievable; fetch-time summary) on police denying mistreatment in the custody death of a foreign transgender activist on Bali, and an August 2026 feature on widening repression - the July 14-16 2026 vigilante wave against trans women (over fifteen doused, stripped and beaten in Bogor, filmed and shared), an October 2025 presidential decree naming "the promotion of LGBTQ+ culture" a non-military security threat, legal gender change conditioned on surgery plus judicial approval, and researchers' accounts of anti-queer attitudes hardening since 2016.

Bengkulu is therefore assessed on national conditions: no criminalisation of identity per se, official framing of visibility as a threat, and vigilante risk with weak accountability - without any documented local divergence in either direction.

records.name: Jambi
records.summary:
The audited sources contain no Jambi-specific finding; they set out the national framework that reaches visitors here: an October 2025 presidential decree listing "the promotion of LGBTQ+ culture" among non-military security threats; legal gender recognition conditioned on sex-reassignment surgery plus judicial approval; a July 14-16 2026 wave of vigilante mob attacks on trans women across the archipelago, concentrated in Bogor where more than fifteen people were doused, stripped and beaten on camera; and 2022 wire reporting, retrieved as a fetch-time summary, of police denying mistreatment after a foreign transgender activist died in Bali custody.

Researchers describe anti-queer attitudes hardening markedly since 2016. In Jambi, the risk profile is that national climate - official framing of visibility as subversive, mob violence with weak accountability, and no criminalisation of identity itself - with no documented local ordinance or protection either way.
